proof_checks.step: Exact sealed statement and public premises
proof_checks.evidence: The complete extracted declaration header matches successor v2 byte-for-byte after ordinary text newline decoding. The only mathematical premises are n>=3, kappa>=4 and ell>=0. Actual Haar, priors, Gaussian constructor, radial test and component expectation are literal let-bindings; no measurable-family, SPD, probability, integrability or desired equality is assumed.

The proof calls the unchanged actual_mixture_laws hn hκ. Its first conjunct supplies Measurable gamma, and its next two conjuncts supply probability of the exact positive/negative bind measures. The inspected parent proves actual Gaussian-family measurability via the exact law-density provider; that provider establishes source precision SPD internally. Measure.bind is join(map), while map defaults to zero only when not a.e. measurable. The candidate supplies global hgamma before lintegral_bind, so the off-measurable branch is never used.

component_probabilities is applied with positive dimension derived from n>=3 and supplies probability for the exact 2*restricted full-Haar measures. orthogonalHaar_spec supplies probability for that same full Haar. No SO replacement, separately chosen conditional law, new normalization or caller probability premise occurs.

Continuity, positivity and norm bound at most one follow from the actual t=exp(-ell*norm(x)^2) and ell>=0. htL proves integrability under every supplied probability measure, including both actual mixtures and every component Gaussian. No strict ell positivity is used. At ell=0 the test is literally one; both probability expectations equal one and the asserted gap is zero.

q(O) is the actual ENNReal integral of ofReal(t) under the canonical gamma(O). Measure.measurable_lintegral composed with established gamma measurability gives measurable q. Component probability and t<=1 prove q<=1 everywhere, hence finite. Nonnegative integral conversion identifies the actual real f(O) with q(O).toReal. Its global measurability and norm bound at most one yield genuine integrability under both priors and full Haar. The norm-integral estimate is not used to hide undefined integration: htL already applies to every component probability.

For an arbitrary probability prior nu, htrans rewrites the actual integral under nu.bind gamma as the toReal of the nonnegative integral, applies Measure.lintegral_bind with established hgamma.aemeasurable and measurable ofReal(t), then integral_toReal with measurable q and its proved everywhere finiteness. The resulting identity concerns actual measures, not a density-only proxy or a characterized law. Final conjunctions separately establish integrability of both spatial and prior integrals, so no Bochner default-zero convention is exploited.

proof_checks.step: Borel sign partition and signed full-Haar split
proof_checks.evidence: Both determinant level sets are Borel by determinant continuity. Determinant of the actual orthogonality identity gives det(O)^2=1, so every full orthogonal matrix has determinant +1 or -1. Pointwise det(O)*f(O) equals the positive indicator times f minus the negative indicator times f. integral_sub uses the two genuinely integrable indicator functions from hfL mu and event measurability; integral_indicator converts to literal restriction integrals.

proof_checks.step: Exact factor two and sign orientation
proof_checks.evidence: integral_smul_measure for the finite ENNReal scalar 2 gives each prior expectation exactly twice its corresponding full-Haar restricted integral. Subtracting positive minus negative therefore equals 2 times the determinant-signed Haar expectation. The final ring step only rearranges these proved real equalities. This is the source relation H=one-half*(Eplus-Eminus), with the correct sign and no missing normalization.

The full candidate has no sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe token and no public helper or new law definition. It does not invoke actual_gaussian_transform or prove the evaluated Eq21 formula, TV inequality, product targets, Poisson estimate, query bound or whole-paper result.
